prerequisites: Mathematical foundation including derivatives, integrals, solving systems of equations, and operations with complex numbers.
Basic knowledge in circuit theory and in analog and digital electronics.
Completion of basic training modules, common to the industrial branch and specific to Industrial Electronic and Automatic Control.

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the specifications and technical literature on communications provided by equipment and software manufacturers.
Understand the operation of different analog and digital modulation systems.
Know the basic structures of electronic communication systems.
Work with radio frequency instrumentation and measure signals in telecommunications.

assessment_methods.method: Report submission and public presentation on a course topic
Laboratory practices (attendance and correct completion of exercises)
Active participation (attitude, participation in theoretical and practical classes, responsiveness, compliance with deadlines)

assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the final grade is calculated as (0.40 x T1) + (0.25 x T2) + (0.25 x PL1) + (0.10 x PA1), provided a minimum of 4.0 points is reached in the theoretical exam (T1) and 5.0 points in the laboratory practices (PL1). Otherwise, the grade will be the minimum between the calculated score and 4.0. For the extraordinary call, the final grade is calculated as (0.70 x T1’) + (0.10 x PL1’), provided a minimum of 5.0 points is reached in the theoretical exam (T1’) and 5.0 points in the practical exam (PL1’). Otherwise, the grade will be the minimum between the calculated score and 4.0. In case of doubt regarding authorship or unauthorized means, an in-person defense may be requested.
